_comment: The DOMAIN vocabulary for keyboard shortcuts. Shared by hotkeys.py (add-ins) and
hotkeys.js (the companion windows), exactly as variables.json is for parameter
names and theme.css is for the look.
A domain is not a hand-declared list of 'these two things never happen together'.
It is a conjunction of AXIS constraints, and mutual exclusivity is then DERIVED:
two actions can share a key  <=>  some axis where both constrain the value
and their allowed values do not overlap
So {sketch: in} and {sketch: out} are exclusive (axis 'sketch', disjoint), and
{command: extrude} and {sketch: in} are exclusive too (an extrude cannot be
running while you are inside a sketch, because 'command' is 'none' there). An
action that constrains nothing is 'always' and excludes nothing, so it can never
share a key. That single rule is what lets the Shortcuts window say yes or no to
a double-up, and EXPLAIN which axis makes it safe.
When two claimants both match at press time (they overlap rather than exclude),
the MORE SPECIFIC one wins - more constrained axes - then higher 'priority',
then the one bound most recently. So a general fallback and a narrow special
case can share a key deliberately.
Adding an axis: add it here, implement its sampler in hotkeys.py::_sample and
mirror it in hotkeys.js. Nothing else needs to know.

workspace.desc: Which Fusion workspace is active. Fusion already disambiguates its OWN shared keys this way; we model it so our actions can join in.
workspace.sample: ui.activeWorkspace.id, folded to the names above

sketch.desc: Whether a sketch is open for editing. The single most useful axis: the sketch environment and the modelling environment are never both live.
sketch.sample: SketchStop.isEnabled, plus the settling stamp - see the sketch-edit-settling-window note

env.desc: DERIVED, not sampled independently: sketch / viewport / dialog, the environments a shortcut's 'Applies in' boxes split between. 'dialog' is ANY of our feature dialogs (Extrude, Mirror, Rectangular Pattern, Combine, Scale... - every command a shared action has a provider for, hotkeys.py::feature_commands, the same set remapd's 'feature' stamp means), never one per command: what a key does INSIDE a dialog is the dialog's own business, said by providing a shared action (Mirror's plane is its Cycle Direction). Otherwise sketch=in gives 'sketch'; anything else gives 'viewport'. Older rows still say `sketch`/`command` instead - `implied_by` is what lets exclusive() compare an env-scoped action against one of those without either side being rewritten. Each entry maps an older constraint to the env values it allows: a value NOT listed here constrains nothing about env. sketch:in allows 'dialog' because Rectangular Pattern runs inside a sketch.
env.sample: command is one of our dialogs -> dialog; elif sketch=in -> sketch; else -> viewport

command.desc: Which Fusion command owns the screen right now, by command id, or 'none' when the app is idle. This is the axis that makes a key mean something INSIDE a command dialog - cycling the extrude operation, say - and nothing outside it.
command.sample: ui.activeCommand, with the idle/selection/nav commands folded to 'none'

focus.desc: Which surface has the keystroke: Fusion's viewport, or one of the companion windows. Lets the same key do the window thing when the window is up and the viewport thing otherwise, without either side hard-coding a letter.
focus.sample: /tmp/fusion_focus, refreshed by whichever companion window holds key focus; stale or missing means viewport

selection.desc: What kind of thing is selected. Coarse on purpose - a key that means one thing with a dimension selected and another with a body selected is a real domain, but finer distinctions belong inside the action, not in the keymap.
selection.sample: the objectType of the first entity in ui.activeSelections
